title: Window manager and damage/redraw
summary: The window manager is the tree's most carefully measured subsystem: synchronous painter's-algorithm repaint with one bounding-box damage rect, a 16-rect clip list and record pointers as the ABI, pushed very far by making every operation repaint only what it provably changed (show/raise reveal nothing, hide/drag repaint a rect, the dither skips ground a window will cover, vacated-rect and shadow-only owing, an opt-in raise cache with explicit promise bits). PERFORMANCE.md Part 5's rows are honoured by the code. The weaknesses are structural: the damage pass still needs a transitive 'redraw everything above a marked window' closure because lower windows are not exactly clipped; two caller-armed one-shot arguments to wm_paint_dmg (npro, stwin) are consumed only on its non-empty path (wm-3); package-supplied window pointers are validated at some doors and not others, and wm_ptr2idx's 8-bit div raises INT 0 on a wild pointer, which on an IBM ROM masks every interrupt (wm-1). Several XT redraw wins (KHP_DMGSTALE/RAISEOL/RELIT/CAPTION) ship only on kern_mega. The source itself is a hazard: 52% comment, much of it per-pass byte history, and about twenty comments or doc passages describe retired designs (the side tables now in the record, wm_fast_ok, 'no do-not-erase flag', bss never zeroed) as current; verification confirmed 28 edits, refuted one, and deferred the duplicated natural-bank banner to wm-14's merge. Nothing needs a big rewrite; the highest-value items are small and ABI-free, and the one big rethink (exact clipping in the damage pass, dropping the closure) is kernel-internal.

strengths.title: wm_pkgcall is the one dispatch site for every window callback
strengths.why: Re-entrant (far pointer read from the record), segment-agnostic (W_SEG=0 kernel window via wm_cbd), package authors never write retf; per-callback pen and depth claim banked on the stack so nested paints inherit nothing. The shape to copy for any new callback kind.

strengths.title: Per-slot state in the record, zeroed when the slot is TAKEN
strengths.why: One rep stosb from W_MENUS to the end kills the stale-handler-in-a-reused-slot class by construction; layout invariants are assembler-checked rather than prose.

strengths.title: Damage engine exactness tricks
strengths.why: Dither minus every frame (phase-correct because the dither is absolute x+y), vacated-rect test, shadow owed as two lines, per-display bands as clip seeds - each removes a double draw for a few bytes.

strengths.title: Derived-not-tracked state and self-healing flags
strengths.why: State that can only be stale in the safe direction (one wasted walk, never a missed timer).

strengths.title: One-shot arguments cleared by the consumer
strengths.why: A caller that forgets inherits the safe default (a wasted repaint, never a missed one). wm-3 is the one gap.

strengths.title: Recursive-aware lock doors
strengths.why: Makes 'call it with or without the gfx lock' true for show/hide/front/resize and closed FIELD-NOTES 34.1's arrow-in-the-cache class.

strengths.title: Preference -> clamp -> floor as one sequence
strengths.why: The three sizing voices cannot be composed differently in two places.

strengths.title: Raise cache with explicit application promises
strengths.why: The application states the fact only it knows; the kernel never guesses, and a covered window keeps the save-under it exists for.

findings.title: wm_ptr2idx raises INT 0 on a wild window pointer; its comment says it is bounded
findings.detail: wm_ptr2idx does sub ax,wm_wins / div cl (CL=WIN_SIZE). The quotient overflows AL - INT 0 - for any BX below wm_wins or more than 255*WIN_SIZE (18,870 bytes) above it. On a 5150/5160 ROM the INT 0 stub masks the 8259 and IRETs: every interrupt gone (instance.inc:1976, wm.inc:8280-8292 already record this). The clamp comment claims a non-window pointer 'names the LAST window ... wrong and bounded' - true only inside that window. Package-facing paths reach it unvalidated: OSAPI_WM_SHOW/HIDE/FRONT (wm_su_precover, wm_zabove), OSAPI_WM_DESTROY, OSAPI_WM_CLIP_SET -> wm_clip_occl -> wm_zabove, the close request. Only inst_wchk (two slots) and wm_isrec (saveu/noanim/quiet) validate. (Precisely: the 8-bit quotient overflows when BX - wm_wins, taken unsigned, is >= 256*WIN_SIZE - 18,944 bytes on kern_big, 16,640 on kern_small - which includes every BX below wm_wins.)
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:7278-7301 the div and the clamp comment
kernel/instance.inc:1975-1979 'div cl FAULTS (int 0, no handler installed)'
kernel/wm.inc:8280-8292 what INT 0 does on an IBM ROM
findings.recommendation: Bound before dividing: cmp ax, MAX_WIN*WIN_SIZE / jae clamp (+5 bytes, ~+8 clocks), or take wm-2 which removes the divide entirely. Fix the comment either way.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: wm_ptr2idx (wm.inc:7278) is sub/div cl with no bound; the kernel installs no INT 0 handler, and wm_title_set's note (8280-8292) records the IBM-ROM mask. OSAPI_WM_DESTROY reaches it twice unvalidated (wm_su_drop -> wm_su_slot, then wm_destroy's own call at 3094); show/hide/front via wm_su_precover/wm_zabove. Correction: the quotient overflows for AX >= 256*WIN_SIZE (18,944 on kern_big, 16,640 on kern_small), not 255*WIN_SIZE; offsets 255*WIN_SIZE..256*WIN_SIZE-1 give AL=255 and are clamped. inst_wchk's own comment has the same off-by-one. Fix cost +5 (cmp ax,imm16 3 + jae 2) is right.

findings.title: Store the slot index in the record so wm_ptr2idx is a load, not a div
findings.detail: Every damage pass calls wm_ptr2idx per marked window (wm_dmg_bit) and wm_idx2ptr per window per walk, O(n^2) in the marking's .mbelow loop; div r8 is 80-90 clocks on the 8088, mul r8 ~70. A byte W_IDX at the record's end, outside wm_create's zero run, written once by wm_init (in .boot2/.ovl, free), makes wm_ptr2idx 'mov al,[bx+W_IDX]/cmp al,MAX_WIN/jb/mov al,MAX_WIN-1/cbw/ret' - 11 bytes vs 19, no divide, no INT 0 (a wild BX reads one byte and is clamped). WIN_SIZE is unpublished, so kernel-internal; tools/os88geom.py's mirror moves with it. A 12-word constant table for wm_idx2ptr (+20 bytes, ~-40 clocks a call) is a separate, record-only trade. Correction: .mbelow tests the mask bit before it calls wm_idx2ptr, so the mul is paid per MARKED lower window, not per pair.
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:5384-5420 .mbelow inner loop with idx2ptr per pair
findings.recommendation: Take with wm-1: add W_IDX (WIN_SIZE 74->75 / 65->66), shorten the create-time zero run by one, fill it in wm_init, rewrite wm_ptr2idx as a bounded load.
findings.bytes_est: -8 .text, +12 .bss kern_big (+6 kern_small): net +4 / -2 resident; ~-80 clocks a call
findings.verify_note: Body sizes check: current wm_ptr2idx is 19 bytes, the bounded load 11 (W_IDX < 128 so disp8). Correction to the detail: the .mbelow loop tests the mask bit first and calls wm_idx2ptr only for a MARKED lower window (wm.inc:5394-5402), so it is not a mul per pair; wm_dmg_bit's div runs once per marked window. WIN_SIZE is unpublished; tools/os88geom.py mirrors it (t_mirror).

findings.title: wm_paint_dmg's empty-rect arm leaks every one-shot argument into the next pass
findings.detail: wm_dmg_npro is consumed only at .promote and wm_dmg_stwin only in wm_dmg_wins' .wdone; the .chrome arm (taken when the clamped rect is empty) reaches neither. (wm_dmg_dk is safe - the entry's word store at wm_dmg_fs clears it - and wm_su_son is armed inside the pass, not by callers.) Callers arm before calling: wm_hide_b sets npro for a desk window, ui_drag sets npro and stwin (via wm_dmg_vacate), desk.inc:978-986 sets stwin=1 with an EMPTY vacated rect plus npro, deskmod.inc:330 sets npro. If such a rect clamps to nothing (a window wholly off the live screen, e.g. after a display removal), the next unrelated pass inherits them: a leaked npro suppresses the next real promotion (front window left with a grey title bar and no grow box), and a leaked stwin makes wm_dmg_stale answer 'clean' for every window that misses the stale vacated rect - with desk's empty rect, every window - so windows the next damage really reached are not redrawn. PLAUSIBLE: requires an empty clamped rect.
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:5468-5481 stwin/su_son/dk cleared only in wm_dmg_wins
findings.recommendation: Clear stwin and npro on the .chrome path too (xor ax,ax / mov [wm_dmg_stwin],ax / mov [wm_dmg_npro],al = 8 bytes, or a shared tail with .wdone), or pass them as a flags argument cleared in one place (see wm-17).
findings.verify_note: Confirmed .chrome (empty clamped rect) reaches neither .promote nor wm_dmg_wins' .wdone, so a caller-armed wm_dmg_npro and wm_dmg_stwin survive into the next pass. Corrections: wm_dmg_dk is NOT leaked - wm_paint_dmg's entry `mov word [wm_dmg_fs], 0` clears fs and dk together (wm.inc:5196, %error 5957); wm_su_son is armed inside a pass (wm_su_sub, 9185/10590) and cleared by wm_draw_win (11087), not by callers before the call. And a leaked stwin=1 (desk.inc:978) cannot make wm_dmg_stale read [1+W_X]: desk arms the vacated rect EMPTY (x2 = 8000h), so gfx_rect_hit fails first and the answer is .clean - i.e. EVERY overlapping window is excused from marking in the next unrelated pass (a missed repaint); a leaked ui_drag stwin excuses every window that missed the stale rect. Reachability stays low (all four arming callers pass on-screen rects).

findings.title: wm_ask_size trusts a W_ONSIZE negotiator to keep BX, which no contract says
findings.detail: wm_ask_size banks AX, SI, BP around wm_pkgcall; its callers write [bx+W_W] straight after. wm_pkgcall restores only DS/ES, and the general rule is 'a window callback may clobber AX-DI and ES'. Neither SPEC.md 11.1 nor the SDK's OSAPI_WM_ONSIZE prose says a negotiator owes BX or DI. The one shipped negotiator (pt_onsize) happens to preserve everything.
evidence: SPEC.md:26382 'may clobber AX/BX/CX/DX/SI/DI/ES like any window callback'
apps/os88api.inc:3178-3192 negotiator contract silent on BX
apps/paint/paint.asm:11758 pt_onsize preserves BX by choice
findings.recommendation: push bx/pop bx in wm_ask_size, and say in the SDK that a negotiator answers in CX/DX and may clobber what any callback may.
findings.verify_note: wm_ask_size (wm.inc:2465) banks only AX/SI/BP around wm_pkgcall, which restores only DS/ES (and the pen words); its own header promises 'every other register preserved'. ui_grow writes [bx+W_W] right after (ui.inc:2243). Evidence correction: the general clobber rule is at SPEC.md:26382 ('may clobber AX/BX/CX/DX/SI/DI/ES like any window callback') and 18329, not 98747.

findings.title: wm_snap_ax moves a window at a LEFT dock's band edge onto the strip (kern_big)
findings.detail: With a left dock, dkx_band sets vid_band_x0 = DOCK_SW = 32. wm_fit floors x at the band edge then calls wm_snap_win; ui_drag snaps a drop the same way. wm_snap_ax rounds the CONTENT origin down: x=32 -> content 33 -> 32 -> frame x=31, which is the strip's rule column. It only special-cases x<7 (jns .fits). The border then overlaps the live strip, so wm_dock_clear (dock_live_hit) answers dirty and every later show/raise/dock update pays wm_dock_under's window repaint - the cost wm_fit's one-pixel rule exists to avoid on a bottom dock. PLAUSIBLE: argued from geometry, not observed.
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:648-661 wm_fit floors x0 then wm_snap_win
kernel/wm.inc:4102-4136 wm_snap_ax rounds down, floor at 0 only
findings.recommendation: In wm_snap_ax (DOCK_OPT arm) compare the rounded x with vid_band_x0 instead of 0 and take the next aligned x up when below.
findings.verify_note: Geometry checks out: dkx_band (dockmod.inc:409-433) sets vid_band_x0 = dock_thk (32) on a left strip whose rect is x 0..31 (SPEC.md 30.5 table); wm_fit floors x at 32 then wm_snap_win; wm_snap_ax rounds the content origin down (33 -> 32 -> frame 31) and only special-cases a negative result; wm_flush_ck suppresses the border only at the display's column 0. wm_zoom's standard rect (x = band_x0) goes through wm_resize's snap the same way, so a zoomed window under a left dock also lands on column 31. Still argued from code, not observed.

findings.title: wm_resize clamps against the union width and ignores the side-dock band
findings.detail: wm_resize_nb clamps width and x against [vid_w] - the virtual desktop width, the union on an extended desktop - and never reads vid_band_x0/xe, while wm_fit and wm_zoom use the band and wm_apply_wh routes multi-display through EXT_APPLY. OSAPI_WM_RESIZE from an app can therefore grow a primary window to straddle the seam, and push a window over a left or right dock strip. PLAUSIBLE: no app shown to do it.
evidence: kernel/viddet.inc:299-307 vid_w is the virtual desktop
findings.recommendation: Clamp with the same band words wm_fit uses on DOCK_OPT, and decide whether the union width is intended on two displays.
findings.verify_note: wm_resize_nb (wm.inc:2495-2545) clamps width and x against [vid_w] (the virtual desktop, viddet.inc:305) and never reads vid_band_x0/xe or EXT_FITBOX, unlike wm_fit (584) and wm_zoom (2899). Plausible, not observed.

findings.title: OSAPI_WM_DESTROY and OSAPI_WM_FULLSCREEN draw without taking the gfx lock
findings.detail: SPEC.md 11.101.2 gave show/hide/front/resize the recursive-aware door because an entry proc runs with the lock free and an unheld repaint banks the arrow into a save-under (FIELD-NOTES 34.1). OSAPI_WM_DESTROY repaints through wm_paint_dmg and OSAPI_WM_FULLSCREEN through wm_raise/wm_paint_all with no door; the SDK justifies destroy's requirement 'as OSAPI_WM_HIDE wants it', no longer true. wm_fullscreen also draws a HIDDEN window whole if called before OSAPI_WM_SHOW (no visible test before wm_raise). wm_lk_go cannot carry fullscreen's CF as written (its or al,al clobbers flags).
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:3321-3352 the four doors through wm_lk_go
kernel/wm.inc:4316-4345 fullscreen enter: no visible test before wm_raise
findings.recommendation: Give destroy the wm_lk_go door (+6). For fullscreen add pushf/popf in wm_lk_go (+2) and a door (+6), and refuse or defer the raise for a hidden window (+~5); or keep the contract and fix the SDK text.
findings.verify_note: Destroy: the SDK (os88api.inc:304) and kernel.asm:3228 both REQUIRE the lock ('the gfx lock is held'), so a destroy without it is a contract violation, not a kernel hazard - the defect is the stale rationale 'as OSAPI_WM_HIDE wants it' (hide takes it itself since 11.101.2); that text is fixed below. Fullscreen: os88api.inc:892-894 says 'caller holds the gfx lock (window callbacks do)' - also a stated contract. wm_lk_go's `or al,al` would indeed clobber CF. The hidden-window draw is real by reading (wm_fullscreen calls wm_raise with no visible test, wm.inc:4325-4331) but unobserved. Severity lowered to low; the door is a consistency choice, not a fix.

findings.title: OSAPI_WM_TIMER with AX >= 32768 fires at once
findings.detail: wm_timer stores [ticks]+AX; the scan fires when [ticks]-W_TIMER is non-negative (sign test). For AX >= 32768 the difference is positive on the next pass, so a 30-60 minute timer fires within a tick. The SDK contract gives no range.
findings.recommendation: Document 'AX <= 32767 ticks (30 minutes)' in the SDK and SPEC.md 13.9, or clamp in wm_timer.
findings.verify_note: wm_timer stores [ticks]+AX (wm.inc:2049); ui.inc:805-812 fires on a non-negative [ticks]-W_TIMER, so AX >= 32768 fires on the next scan. Neither os88api.inc:3231ff nor SPEC.md 13.9 states a range. Note OSAPI_WM_TIMER's body is inside the KERN_BIG arm.

findings.title: wm_su_drop ignores mem_free's refusal and loses the claim
findings.detail: wm_su_drop zeroes the slot word then calls mem_free; mem_free_x refuses (CF=1) while a compaction relocation walk is busy. The cache claim is then owned and unreachable. Reachable only if a drop happens inside a relocation proc (a package proc calling OSAPI_WM_CLIP_SET or SAVEU).
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:9866-9888 and word [si],0 before mem_free, CF ignored
findings.recommendation: Clear the slot only on CF=0, or state that relocation procs may not call clip/saveu.
findings.verify_note: wm_su_drop zeroes the slot then ignores mem_free's CF (wm.inc:9880-9882); mem_free_x refuses under mem_cp_busy (memory.inc:4446). But SPEC.md 66.3 author rule 3 (line 118315) already forbids a relocation proc to 'claim, free, resize, yield, draw', so the path needs a package to break a binding rule; the 'or state that relocation procs may not call clip/saveu' half is essentially already written. Robustness only.

findings.title: wm_lk's gfx_lock_flag test is redundant
findings.detail: gfx_unlock stamps gfx_lock_own = 0xFF before dropping the flag, so owner==sch_cur already implies held; wm_lk's 'free' and 'other' outcomes are the same wm_lk_take, so the leading cmp/je pair can go. fpg_arm partitions the states differently and keeps its test, as wm_lk's own comment notes.
findings.recommendation: Delete cmp byte [gfx_lock_flag],0 / je wm_lk_take.
findings.verify_note: gfx_unlock ends with `mov word [gfx_lock_flag], 0xFF00` (vga12.inc:5258, owner 0xFF and flag 0 in one store) and gfx_lock writes flag+owner in one word store; the only other writers of the flag (KFZTRACE strip, kern_mega's fault strip) restore it or halt. So owner == sch_cur implies held, and the leading cmp byte [mem],0 / je (5+2 = 7 bytes) is redundant. -7 is right.

findings.title: The XT does not get the redraw knobs built and measured for it
findings.detail: KHP_DMGSTALE (+38, drags over hidden windows -12 to -32%), KHP_RAISEOL (+90, CGA raise -5 to -14 ms), KHP_RELIT (+32, fullscreen exit 781->629 ms CGA) and KHP_CAPTION (+34) are kern_mega only, which runs on 286/386 VGA machines where these milliseconds matter least; the measurements are 4.77 MHz XT. Meanwhile wm.inc carries both arms of wm_dmg_stale, wm_raise, wm_draw_win and wm_cov_rect indefinitely.
evidence: kernel/kernel.asm:283-294 KHP defines in the KERN_MEGA block
findings.recommendation: Decide each for kern_big against its bytes (+194 for all four) and delete the losing arm; a knob not shipped on the target is a second source tree in the hottest file.
findings.verify_note: kernel.asm:283-294 defines KHP_RELIT/CAPTION/DMGSTALE/RAISEOL under %ifdef KERN_MEGA only; LAST-DROP-PERF.md 7.1 rows 2/4/5/7 carry them (+32/+38/+34/+90) as a pending decision. Already listed, as the reviewer says.

findings.title: Transitive marking redraws windows that were never damaged
findings.detail: wm_dmg_wins marks a window that merely overlaps a marked window below it, because the lower one is redrawn WHOLE (unclipped except by the cull) and would paint over it. Vacated-rect and DMGSTALE keep the first link short, but one marked window at the bottom of a cascade still repaints the cascade (Part 5's widget-drop row). The marking loop is O(n^2) over z-order pairs, with a mul and an overlap test per MARKED lower window. Cheap intermediate: clip each marked window's draw to its visible region (the 11.97 chrome clip already does this for the outline, the 11.3.3 cull for W_PAINT) and mark an upper window only when it meets the lower window's VISIBLE region intersected with the damage.
evidence: PERFORMANCE.md Part 5 widget-drop row ('every ordinary window over its old or new rect redrawn WHOLE')
findings.recommendation: Count .mbelow hits on MartyPC first (one rebuild), then prototype the visible-region predicate behind a knob. See Rethink R1 in the report.
findings.verify_note: The closure is as described (wm.inc:5384-5420: a window is marked when it overlaps any marked window below). Correction: the inner loop tests the mask bit first, so wm_idx2ptr's mul and wm_ovl run only per marked lower window, not 'a mul per inner step'. Byte estimate unmeasured, as stated.

findings.title: Window-pointer validation is inconsistent across the wm doors
findings.detail: wm_saveu/wm_noanim/wm_quiet (wm_isrec), wm_ownseg and two inst_wchk slots validate BX; SHOW/HIDE/FRONT/DESTROY/CLIP_SET/BAND/OWNBG/KEEPH/SNAP/SIZABLE do not, and the inline setter cells (mov [cs:bx+W_ONCLICK],ax/retf) cannot - BX=0 there writes the kernel's first 74 bytes of .text. A policy question: the tree trusts packages but spends bytes validating at some doors.
findings.recommendation: Write the rule into SPEC.md 11: either BX is trusted at every door (remove the inconsistent checks) or one shared validating prologue for the RSLOT doors. wm-1/wm-2 make the shared funnel safe regardless.
findings.verify_note: wm_isrec (11672, a bound only), wm_saveu/noanim/quiet and inst_wchk validate; wm_band, show/hide/front, destroy, clip_set and the inline setter cells (mov [cs:bx+W_*],ax / retf at wm.inc:1519-2156, kernel.asm:3517/3551) do not. A policy question, correctly framed.

findings.title: wm_dmg_bands and the natural-bank banner exist twice, with dead inner arms
findings.detail: DOCK_OPT == KERN_BIG, so the %ifdef KERN_BIG inside the DOCK_OPT copy has a dead %else and the one inside the non-DOCK_OPT copy a dead %if; the copies differ by the six-line side-band clamp. Two 60-line banners to keep true (both already stale, mismatch 9).
findings.recommendation: One body with %ifdef DOCK_OPT around the six lines.
findings.verify_note: kernel.asm:1263 defines DOCK_OPT iff KERN_BIG; wm.inc:813-962 and 963-1104 differ only by the side-band clamp (diffed). Merging them also makes the stale natural-bank banner (doc mismatch 11) uniquely editable.

findings.title: wm.inc narrates its own history and the narration goes stale
findings.detail: 12,041 lines, 6,235 pure comment; much is per-instruction history ('kernel size pass 15, -2', commented-out stores at 3113-3150). 22 comments/doc passages describe retired designs as current (the pass-4 side tables alone account for eight). The rationale is valuable; the byte ledger belongs in git log and the KSP reports, which already carry it.
findings.recommendation: A comment pass: keep contracts, invariants and why; drop pass ledgers and commented-out code; apply the mismatch fixes.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: commented-out clears at wm.inc:3113-3150 and the side-table banners at 1545/2089/2112/2139/2823 are as described (fixed below).

findings.title: The content white fill is still the default double-draw
findings.detail: wm_draw_win fills content white before W_PAINT unless WF_OWNBG - the erase-then-draw pattern CLAUDE.md calls canonical. About 29 package directories (assembly and C) name OSAPI_WM_OWNBG / os88_wm_ownbg (grep), out of ~70 under apps/. This is Windows' WM_ERASEBKGND with a default brush; the opt-out is the right shape and the rest is a queue.
evidence: grep: 32 asm + 9 C packages call OSAPI_WM_OWNBG / os88_wm_ownbg
findings.recommendation: Make OWNBG the documented expectation (docs/INDEX.md, porting skills) and keep a ratchet list of non-callers like tests/movable.txt. No kernel change.
findings.verify_note: The default fill and the opt-out are as described (wm.inc:11017-11030). The counts could not be reproduced: grep finds WM_OWNBG/wm_ownbg named in about 29 package directories (asm and C together, hosttests excluded) out of ~70 under apps/; treat '32 asm + 9 C' as approximate.

findings.title: One-shot arguments to the damage pass are globals with many lifetimes
findings.detail: wm_dmg_mine cleared by wm_raise, wm_dmg_rzwin by wm_resize_nb, dk/stwin/su_son by wm_dmg_wins, npro by .promote, cullq by wm_dmg_wins's bracket, cvf_on by wm_draw_win. Each was right when written; as a set they are an implicit calling convention a new early-out can break (wm-3).
findings.recommendation: One flags byte plus the rect words, cleared in ONE place at wm_paint_dmg's exit.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked the lifetimes: wm_dmg_mine cleared/armed in wm_raise (3489), wm_dmg_rzwin by wm_resize_nb (2591-2595), dk/stwin/su_son at .wdone (5523-5525), npro at .promote (5285), su_son also by wm_draw_win (11087). Note dk is additionally cleared at entry with wm_dmg_fs.

findings.title: The clip region is a 16-rect list with no coalescing
findings.detail: wm_clip_split replaces a rect with up to four fragments and never merges neighbours; at 16 each caller degrades (clip_set skips the frame, gray dithers all, covered draws anyway). QuickDraw/X11 Y-X banded regions keep above/below strips full width and merge equal bands. Overflow frequency on a 12-window desktop is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Counter in wm_clip_add's .full (one rebuild) before changing anything.
findings.prior_art: Mac QuickDraw regions; X11 Y-X banded regions
findings.verify_note: Low-severity record item; not re-verified.

findings.title: band.inc: 1,634 bytes for a title bar that is slower on VGA (knob only)
findings.detail: The composer measured 36.5 vs 40.8 ms (Hercules), 37.1 vs 42.0 (CGA), 38.3 vs 30.3 (VGA) for 1,634 bytes; code read clean (clip, polarity, replay). Since the caption's one-font_run_x path took most of the double-write out of the default bar, its remaining argument is the stripes. No shipped kernel assembles it.
findings.recommendation: Retire BAND=1 and its buildmatrix row, or keep it explicitly as a reference implementation.
findings.verify_note: kernel.asm:904-908: BANDCOMP is defined only under BAND (a knob) on KERN_BIG; no shipped kernel assembles band.inc.

findings.title: wm_anim yields while holding the gfx lock
findings.detail: wm_anim loops task_yield for every frame of the zoom with the caller's lock held; workers block for the whole animation (~WM_ANIM_N x 27.5 ms). Deliberate (the XOR outline must not be overdrawn) but the one place the WM holds the screen across a scheduling point, and SPEC.md 11.99 does not say so.
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:3386-3388 called from wm_show_b under the lock
findings.recommendation: State it in SPEC.md 11.99.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md 11.99 already says it: 'The lock is HELD across the wait' and wm_anim's frame wait task_yields (SPEC.md:25441-25445). Nothing to add.

findings.title: Exact clipping in the damage pass, dropping the painter's-algorithm closure
findings.detail: Mac and Windows never redraw an undamaged window above a damaged one: each draws only into visRgn intersect updateRgn, in any order. os8088 is most of the way there (outline clipped 11.97, W_PAINT under the cull 11.3.3, glyph rows 11.3.2 and columns 11.3.4 on kern_big, icons 11.3.5). What still forces the closure is the cull rounding a cell OUTWARD and gfx_blit4/gfx_scroll taking no clip (SPEC.md 11.3's named holes). Kernel-internal, no ABI.
findings.recommendation: Prototype behind a knob, measured on MartyPC: an inward-rounding cull when the window above will not be redrawn, plus clip support for blit4/scroll; then drop .mbelow.
findings.prior_art: Mac QuickDraw BeginUpdate; Windows BeginPaint/update region; GEOS mask regions
findings.verify_note: The named holes exist (SPEC.md 18993 'Two are still holes'; 11.3.3 is 'the one pass that may round a cell OUTWARD'). A design proposal, unmeasured, as stated.

findings.title: Deferred invalidation (WM_PAINT / update regions)
findings.detail: Every wm operation repaints synchronously. A per-window owed rect accumulated by damage and drained once per UI pass would coalesce sequences that repaint twice today (task-owned close: hide then destroy; several OSAPI_WM_RESIZE in one handler; drop then ONRESIZE relayout). Callers that rely on pixels being on the glass at return (raise-cache take-after-draw) need auditing. OS/2's CS_SYNCPAINT shows how to introduce it opt-in.
evidence: kernel/wm.inc:5128-5145 the empty-rect special case exists for hide-then-destroy
findings.recommendation: Write a plan; default sync, opt-in deferred per window.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x InvalidateRect/WM_PAINT; OS/2 PM CS_SYNCPAINT; Mac update events
findings.verify_note: Low-severity record item; not re-verified.

findings.title: Window handles instead of record pointers in the ABI
findings.detail: Raw record pointers are why validation is inconsistent (wm-13) and why the funnel was dangerous (wm-1). A slot-index handle validated by one cmp at every door ends the class, but packages read W_X..W_H via [es:bx+...] in hundreds of places, so it breaks every package. wm-1/wm-2 get the safety for ~5 bytes without it.
evidence: SPEC.md 11 'The record lives in KERNEL_SEG ... through an es: override'
findings.recommendation: Record only; if R6 (content coordinates, design B) is ever taken, take this with it.
findings.listed_as: pairs with ABI-BREAK-LIST R6 and K17-2/K17-3
findings.verify_note: Low-severity flag-day record item; not re-verified.
